rationale: The conditioning logic is internally consistent (indicator fires exactly when oancf < capx) and the external-finance-dependence channel is a defensible sharpening of the asset-growth anomaly, but the design leaves a large point mass at exactly zero for self-funded firms, which will degenerate quantile breakpoints and make the reported spread partly a "FCF-negative vs. everyone else" sort rather than a growth sort — worth testing, but diagnose the zero-mass before believing the alpha.

Because RANK is non-negative the volatility term only attenuates, never flips, asset growth, so the signal is close to a monotone re-weighting of the Cooper-Gulen-Schill asset-growth anomaly (and the well-documented investment × uncertainty interaction) and will likely be highly collinear with plain GROWTH(at,1) rather than an independent cross-theme effect.

Net-debt-issuance underperformance is itself published, but conditioning issuance on cash-flow coverage of total liabilities is a specific and economically coherent distress/overinvestment refinement with the right sign orientation; watch for lt near zero and for correlation with plain net debt issuance in the diagnostics.

This is the most genuinely conditional construction of the set — the sign flip on the multi-year gross-margin trend makes identical capex intensity map to opposite tails, which is a real test of productive vs. unproductive expansion rather than a re-weighted investment factor — though discarding trend magnitude via SIGN is coarse and the positive expected sign is a bold bet against the unconditional investment effect, so it must be verified that the long leg is not just high-profitability firms.

The expression is the product of two non-negative terms so most firms (non-acquirers) sit at exactly zero, meaning the sort collapses to acquirer-vs-non-acquirer and the signal is essentially the mechanical intersection of two established anomalies (acquirer underperformance and accruals) rather than a new interaction.

Inventory growth in excess of sales growth is a long-standing Abarbanell-Bushee/Thomas-Zhang fundamental signal and the non-negative ROA rank only attenuates rather than reorders it, so this is a modest refinement rather than a novel mechanism — acceptable to test only if it is shown to add cross-sectional information beyond the raw inventory-sales wedge.
